extracted.intended_audience: readers and writers of comic, digressive 18th-century fiction; literary scholars and creative-writers studying Laurence Sterne's techniques
extracted.subtask_description: Producing or analyzing comic, highly digressive 18th-century novelistic prose that mixes satire, rhetoric, and self-conscious commentary. Emphasis on originality, provocation, associative meaning, and playful chapter-structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality vs. mere accumulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell me, ye learned, shall we for ever be adding so much to the bulk—so little to the stock? Are we for ever to be twisting, and untwisting the same rope? — critique of producing books that merely replicate existing material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid producing work that only increases 'bulk' without adding substantive new contribution. Do not imitate or rework received materials without generating fresh insight or effect; aim to 'work one miracle' with learning rather than merely display relics of it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of learning should produce novelty, not showy display
rubrics_metrics.description: Shall we be shewing the relics of learning, as monks do the relics of their saints—without working one miracle with them? — admonition against empty display of erudition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When invoking classical, historical, or learned material, integrate it to produce new effects or arguments rather than as ostentatious citation. Learning should be employed inventively to advance the work's purpose, not merely to ornament or signal scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an energetic, life-giving effect (True Shandeism)
rubrics_metrics.description: True Shandeism... opens the heart and lungs, and ... forces the blood and other vital fluids of the body to run freely through its channels, makes the wheel of life run long and cheerfully round.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for prose that enlivens the reader—evoking cheerfulness, emotional openness, and vivacity. The comic voice should have a restorative, spirited effect rather than producing flat irony or deadening cleverness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boldness and candid language (willingness to offend)
rubrics_metrics.description: I shall not be at all nice in the choice of my words!... depend upon’t I’ll give you something, my good gentry, next year to be offended at — authorial declaration to use frank/impertinent language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit candid, indelicate, or provocative diction when it serves comic or rhetorical ends. Expect and accept that deliberate offense or shock may be part of the work's strategy; discretion may be set aside for effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of associative meanings and social reception
rubrics_metrics.description: The discussion in the 'Whiskers' fragment shows how a single word acquires indecency or new meanings by association—extremes of delicacy and the beginnings of concupiscence hold their next provincial chapter together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be attentive to how words, images, or motifs carry associative baggage in social contexts; a seemingly innocent term can become charged by usage and rumor. Consider how audiences might interpret associations and the resulting moral/social reception of your language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid mimicry — satirize imitators
rubrics_metrics.description: I wish from my soul, that every imitator in Great Britain, France, and Ireland, had the farcy for his pains; and that there was a good farcical house, large enough to hold—shag rag and bob-tail, male and female, all together — visceral attack on literary imitators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate an individual voice rather than copying prevailing fashions or famous authors. The passage endorses satirizing or scorning mere imitators; originality of temperament and method is a positive criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace digression and metafictional play
rubrics_metrics.description: The narrator explicitly plans chapters (the chapter of THINGS; the chapter upon WHISKERS) and announces structural asides and promises to the reader—self-conscious commentary on form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use digressions, chapter-naming, direct addresses to readers, and self-referential remarks as legitimate techniques. Structural playfulness (interrupting, teasing future chapters, naming 'things') is part of the comic narrative strategy and can be used deliberately to shape tone and expectation.
